claim: Cardiac sympathetic axons from the right STG descend along the right superior vena cava to reach and innervate the sinoatrial (SA) node and the lateral surface of the ventricles.
source: Specifically, cardiac sympathetic axons from the right STG descend along the right superior vena cava to reach and innervate the sinoatrial (SA) node and the lateral surface of the ventricles
evidence: This is a descriptive anatomical claim based on the authors' observations and previous work.

claim: Cardiac sympathetic axons from the left STG extend along the left superior vena cava, the left sinus horn, the sinus venosus, and project further onto the dorsal surface of the ventricular chamber.
source: while those from the left STG extend along the left superior vena cava, the left sinus horn, the sinus venosus, and project further onto the dorsal surface of the ventricular chamber.
evidence: This is a descriptive anatomical claim based on the authors' observations and previous work.

claim: Endothelin-1 (Edn1) is selectively expressed by the endothelium of the cardiac veins.
source: we previously demonstrated that endothelin-1 (Edn1), which is selectively expressed by the endothelium of the cardiac veins, directs axonal growth towards and along these venous routes by the subset of STG neurons (approx. 50%) that express the endothelin receptor Ednra (Manousiouthakis et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Approximately 50% of STG neurons express the endothelin receptor Ednra.
source: directs axonal growth towards and along these venous routes by the subset of STG neurons (approx. 50%) that express the endothelin receptor Ednra (Manousiouthakis et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Axons from the STG initiate extension toward the heart at embryonic day (E) 14.5 in mice.
source: In mice, axons from the STG initiate extension toward the heart at embryonic day (E) 14.5 and have reached the heart by E15.5.
evidence: This is a temporal observation about developmental timing.

claim: Axons from the STG have reached the heart by E15.5 in mice.
source: In mice, axons from the STG initiate extension toward the heart at embryonic day (E) 14.5 and have reached the heart by E15.5.
evidence: This is a temporal observation about developmental timing.

claim: Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient mouse embryos showed a significant reduction of cardiac sympathetic axons reaching the SA node and the ventricular myocardium at E15.5.
source: The functional role of endothelin signaling was demonstrated in Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient mouse embryos, which showed a significant reduction of cardiac sympathetic axons reaching the SA node and the ventricular myocardium at E15.5.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mutant mice.

claim: The deficiency of sympathetic innervation in Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient mice persisted into the postnatal period.
source: This deficiency of sympathetic innervation persisted into the postnatal period, and as a consequence, mutant mice were substantially compromised in ionotropic response to sympathetic activation (i.e., amphetamine-induced increased heart rate).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mutant mice.

claim: Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient mutant mice were substantially compromised in ionotropic response to sympathetic activation (amphetamine-induced increased heart rate).
source: This deficiency of sympathetic innervation persisted into the postnatal period, and as a consequence, mutant mice were substantially compromised in ionotropic response to sympathetic activation (i.e., amphetamine-induced increased heart rate).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mutant mice.

claim: Venous endothelium-derived Edn1 induces the ability of Ednra+ sympathetic axons to repel from competing arterial routes by upregulating the expression of Plexin-A4 in Ednra+ STG neurons.
source: We demonstrate that venous endothelium-derived Edn1 not only instructs Ednra+ sympathetic axon guidance to the heart, but also induces the ability of these axons to repel from competing arterial routes by upregulating the expression of Plexin-A4 in Ednra+ STG neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Edn1-Ednra signaling-deficient STG complexes abnormally project medially across the dorsal wall of the thoracic cavity and ultimately reach the descending aorta.
source: We found that Edn1-Ednra signaling-deficient STG complexes also abnormally project medially across the dorsal wall of the thoracic cavity, and ultimately reach the descending aorta
evidence: This claim is supported by wholemount Th immunostaining data shown in Figure 1b-d and i.

claim: Ectopic projections from Edn1-Ednra signaling-deficient STGs were associated with the posterior intercostal arteries and the right subclavian artery.
source: Histological analyses showed that these ectopic projections were associated with the posterior intercostal arteries and the right subclavian artery, which are visceral branches of the thoracic aorta
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1j-q.

claim: Wild-type thoracic aortic segments exhibited a strong attractive effect on wild-type STG neurite outgrowth in collagen gel co-culture.
source: Similar to the response to venous segments, wild-type thoracic aortic segments exhibited a strong attractive effect on wild-type STG neurite outgrowth
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 2a and c.

claim: A large fraction of control neurites in the proximal quadrant either stopped midway to the aortic segment or turned away from the aortic segment in collagen gel co-culture.
source: However, unlike the response to the venous segments, a large fraction of control neurites in the proximal quadrant either stopped midway to the aortic segment (Figure 2a yellow dot, 2d) or turned away from the aortic segment (Figure 2a red dots, 2d).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 2a and d.

claim: A much greater fraction of Ednra-deficient neurites grew into or turned towards the aortic segments compared to controls in collagen gel co-culture.
source: Interestingly, however, a much greater fraction of Ednra-deficient neurites grew into or turned towards the aortic segments (Figure 2b blue dots; Figure 2d blue bars), and reciprocally, fewer neurites stopped or turned away from the aortic segment (Figure 2b and d).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 2b and d.

claim: The thoracic aorta expresses factor(s) that are repulsive for a subset of sympathetic axons of the STGs.
source: These observations collectively suggest that, in addition to tropic and trophic factors, the thoracic aorta also expresses factor(s) that are repulsive for a subset of sympathetic axons of the STGs
evidence: This is an inference based on the in vitro explant culture data.

claim: Ednra is intrinsically required in STG neurons to respond to repulsive guidance cue(s) emanating from the thoracic aorta.
source: and furthermore, that Ednra is intrinsically required in these STG neurons to respond to these repulsive guidance cue(s) emanating from the thoracic aorta.
evidence: This is an inference based on the in vitro explant culture data.

claim: In all Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient STGs, Plxna4 expression was reduced by half.
source: In all Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient STGs, Plxna4 expression was reduced by half, whereas expression of Nrp1 and Plxna3 was unaffected.
evidence: This claim is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Expression of Nrp1 and Plxna3 was unaffected in Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient STGs.
source: In all Edn1-Ednra signaling deficient STGs, Plxna4 expression was reduced by half, whereas expression of Nrp1 and Plxna3 was unaffected.
evidence: This claim is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: In control embryos, Plexin-A4 was detected in Th+ cardiac sympathetic axons that descended along the superior vena cavae.
source: Indeed, in control embryos, Plexin-A4 was detected in Th+ cardiac sympathetic axons that descended along the superior vena cavae (Figure 3d–e,h–i).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3d-e and h-i.

claim: In littermate Ednra mutant embryos, there was no detectable level of Plexin-A4 expression in sympathetic axons that misprojected along the thoracic aorta and the intercostal arteries.
source: In littermate Ednra mutant embryos, there was no detectable level of Plexin-A4 expression in sympathetic axons that misprojected along the thoracic aorta and the intercostal arteries (Figure 3j–k and l–m, yellow arrows)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3j-k and l-m.

claim: Axons associated with the superior vena cavae retained Plexin-A4 expression in Ednra mutant embryos.
source: whereas axons associated with the superior vena cavae retained Plexin-A4 expression (Figure 3j–k and l–m, white arrowheads).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3j-k and l-m.

claim: Venous Edn1 is an upstream regulator of Plxna4 gene expression within Ednra+ cardiac STG neurons.
source: These results suggest that venous Edn1 is an upstream regulator of Plxna4 gene expression within Ednra+ cardiac STG neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data.

claim: The Plxna4 gene contains a highly conserved MEF2 binding site ~50 kb upstream of the transcription start site.
source: Using these two complementary approaches, we found a highly conserved MEF2 binding site ~50 kb upstream of the transcription start site (TSS) and four highly conserved MEF2 binding sites located in the third intron of Plxna4 gene (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by bioinformatics analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The Plxna4 gene contains four highly conserved MEF2 binding sites located in the third intron.
source: Using these two complementary approaches, we found a highly conserved MEF2 binding site ~50 kb upstream of the transcription start site (TSS) and four highly conserved MEF2 binding sites located in the third intron of Plxna4 gene (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by bioinformatics analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Robust upregulation of Plxna4 gene expression was observed in Edn1-treated control neural crest-derived cells.
source: Importantly, we observed robust upregulation of Plxna4 gene expression in Edn1-treated control neural crest-derived cells (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-sequencing data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: In the absence of Mef2c function in the neural crest, Edn1 induction of Plxna4 expression was significantly attenuated compared to Edn1 induction of Plxna4 expression in control neural crest.
source: In the absence of Mef2c function in the neural crest, Edn1 induction of Plxna4 expression was significantly attenuated compared to Edn1 induction of Plxna4 expression in control neural crest (Figure 4b)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-sequencing data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Ectopic medial projections from the STG towards the dorsal aorta were observed in Mef2c mutant embryos.
source: Indeed, we observed ectopic medial projections from the STG (including T1 through T3 sympathetic chain segments) towards the dorsal aorta in Mef2c mutant embryos (Figure 4c–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by wholemount Th immunostaining data shown in Figure 4c-d.

claim: Axons associated with the superior vena cavae retained Plexin-A4 expression in Mef2cNCKO mutant embryos.
source: Just as observed in Ednra mutants (Figure 3b–m), axons associated with the superior vena cavae retained Plexin-A4 expression in Mef2cNCKO mutant embryos (Figure 4f and i–j).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4f and i-j.

claim: Sympathetic axons associated with the thoracic aorta did not express Plexin-A4 in Mef2cNCKO mutant embryos.
source: In contrast, sympathetic axons associated with the thoracic aorta did not express Plexin-A4 in Mef2cNCKO mutant embryos (Figure 4f and k–l)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4f and k-l.

claim: The extent of sympathetic innervation of the heart is compromised in Th-Cre; Ednrafl/- conditional null mice.
source: As we described previously (Manousiouthakis et al., 2014), the extent of sympathetic innervation of the heart is compromised in Th-Cre; Ednrafl/- conditional null mice (Figure 5d, Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by wholemount immunostaining data shown in Figure 5d and Figure 5—figure supplement 1a.

claim: A similar degree of impairment in sympathetic innervation was observed in sympathetic-neuron-specific Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/- double heterozygous mice.
source: We observed a similar degree of impairment in sympathetic-neuron-specific Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/- double heterozygous mice (Figure 5c, Figure 5—figure supplement 1a–b).
evidence: This claim is supported by wholemount immunostaining data shown in Figure 5c and Figure 5—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: Th+ nerve fibers were reduced in number and caliber in double heterozygous hearts at the SA node.
source: In sections through the SA node, using HCN4 as a marker of conduction system cardiomyocytes, Th+ nerve fibers were obviously reduced in number and caliber, although still present, in double heterozygous hearts (Figure 5k, Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5k and Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The level of Syp staining was reduced commensurate with the reduction of Th staining in double heterozygous hearts.
source: The level of Syp staining was reduced commensurate with the reduction of Th staining (Figure 5l–m, Figure 5—figure supplement 1b)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5l-m and Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Mice heterozygous at the Ednra or Plxna4 loci individually responded normally to amphetamine in the acute period by increasing heart rate.
source: Mice heterozygous at the Ednra or Plxna4 loci individually responded normally to amphetamine in the acute period (<2 min after injection) by increasing heart rate (Figure 6a)
evidence: This claim is supported by ECG data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Ednra; Plxna4 double heterozygous mice exhibited a severely blunted acute ionotropic response to amphetamine.
source: However, Ednra; Plxna4 double heterozygous mice (Ednra+/-; Plxna4+/-) and conditional Ednra-Plxna4 double-heterozygous mice (Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/-) exhibited a severely blunted acute ionotropic response, nearing the completely eliminated response of homozygous sympathetic-neuron-specific Ednra mutants (Th-Cre; Ednrafl/-) (Figure 6a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ECG data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Conditional Ednra-Plxna4 double-heterozygous mice exhibited a severely blunted acute ionotropic response to amphetamine.
source: However, Ednra; Plxna4 double heterozygous mice (Ednra+/-; Plxna4+/-) and conditional Ednra-Plxna4 double-heterozygous mice (Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/-) exhibited a severely blunted acute ionotropic response, nearing the completely eliminated response of homozygous sympathetic-neuron-specific Ednra mutants (Th-Cre; Ednrafl/-) (Figure 6a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ECG data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The delayed response to amphetamine (monitored 10 min after injection) was fully intact in all double-heterozygous mice.
source: This delayed response (monitored 10 min after injection) was fully intact in all double-heterozygous mice (Figure 6b)
evidence: This claim is supported by ECG data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Double-heterozygous mice were normally responsive to the beta-adrenergic receptor agonist isoproterenol.
source: Furthermore, these mice were normally responsive to the beta-adrenergic receptor agonist isoproterenol (Figure 6c)
evidence: This claim is supported by ECG data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: In Th-Cre; Ednrafl/- mutants, a significant reduction of the LF component was observed.
source: In Th-Cre; Ednrafl/- mutants, in which sympathetic innervation and activity are reduced (Figure 5d, n–p and w–x), a significant reduction of the LF component was observed (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 1c)
evidence: This claim is supported by heart rate variability analysis shown in Figure 6d and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/- mice exhibited a similar reduction of the LF/HF ratio as Th-Cre; Ednrafl/- mutants.
source: Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/- ± also exhibited a similar reduction of the LF/HF ratio (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 1b)
evidence: This claim is supported by heart rate variability analysis shown in Figure 6d and Figure 6—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Amphetamine treatment increases the LF/HF ratio in normal mice by activating sympathetic activity.
source: Amphetamine treatment increases the LF/HF ratio in normal mice by activating sympathetic activity, but this did not change in the compound mutants
evidence: This claim is supported by heart rate variability analysis shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Plxna4 mutants show an SCG misprojection phenotype that results in fewer SCG axons extending along the external carotid arteries.
source: Plxna4 mutants show an SCG misprojection phenotype (Waimey et al., 2008) that results in fewer SCG axons extending along the external carotid arteries (Figure 7c and g).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 7c and g, and citation to previous work.

claim: Ednra-Plxna4 double heterozygotes were unaffected in SCG external carotid artery projection.
source: Interestingly, however, Ednra-Plxna4 double heterozygotes were unaffected in SCG external carotid artery projection (Figure 7b and f).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 7b and f.

claim: Sema3a and Sema3f are both expressed by the dermomyotome, forelimbs and paraxial mesoderm during the E10.5–12.5 period.
source: Sema3a and Sema3f are both expressed by the dermomyotome, forelimbs and paraxial mesoderm during the E10.5–12.5 period (Kawasaki et al., 2002; Maden et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Sema3a and Sema3f mutant embryos independently display medial ectopic projections from sympathetic ganglia in the upper thorax.
source: and Sema3a and Sema3f mutant embryos independently display medial ectopic projections from sympathetic ganglia in the upper thorax (Maden et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Selective expression of Sema3a and Sema3f was confirmed in the smooth muscle layer of the upper thoracic aorta during the critical period of cardiac sympathetic axonal extension to the heart.
source: We confirmed selective expression of Sema3a and Sema3f in the smooth muscle layer of the upper thoracic aorta during the critical period of cardiac sympathetic axonal extension to the heart (Figure 8—figure supplement 1a–d and e–h).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1a-d and e-h.

claim: STG isolated from E14.5 control embryos and explanted alone do not extend neurites in minimal growth medium with no growth/trophic factors added.
source: As noted above, in minimal growth medium with no growth/trophic factors added, STG isolated from E14.5 control embryos and explanted alone do not extend neurites (Manousiouthakis et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: STG exhibited a robust tropic and trophic response to aggregates of untransfected COS cells, regardless of Ednra or Plxna4 genotype.
source: Regardless of Ednra or Plxna4 genotype, STG exhibited a robust tropic and trophic response to aggregates of untransfected COS cells, indicating that COS cells secrete factors (which are not defined) that are active on sympathetic neurons (Figure 8a–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 8a-d.

claim: When control STGs were placed between untransfected and Sema3a-transfected COS cell aggregates, neurites only projected away from the Sema3a-expressing cells.
source: When control STGs were placed between untransfected and Sema3a-transfected COS cell aggregates (GFP+) (Figure 8i), neurites only projected away from the Sema3a-expressing cells (Figure 8e and j)
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 8e, i, and j.

claim: Neurites from Ednra+/- or Plxna4+/- STGs showed a similar response to Sema3a-expressing COS aggregates as control STGs.
source: Neurites from Ednra+/- or Plxna4+/- STGs showed a similar response to Sema3a-expressing COS aggregates as control STGs (Figure 8j).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 8j.

claim: Ednra-deficient STGs exhibited a fraction of neurite outgrowth that was attracted towards the Sema3a-expressing COS aggregate.
source: In contrast, however, Ednra-deficient STGs exhibited a fraction of neurite outgrowth that was attracted towards the Sema3a-expressing COS aggregate (Figure 8g and j).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 8g and j.

claim: A similar response to Sema3a-expressing COS aggregates was observed in Ednra-Plxna4 double heterozygote STG and Plxna4-null-STG explants.
source: A similar response was observed in Ednra-Plxna4 double heterozygote STG and Plxna4-null-STG explants (Figure 8f, h and j).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro explant culture data shown in Figure 8f, h, and j.

claim: Cardiac sympathetic axons from the STGs are unique in following veins to reach the heart, while sympathetic axons follow arteries in virtually all other cases.
source: While sympathetic axons follow arteries in virtually all other cases, we discovered that cardiac sympathetic axons from the STGs are unique in following veins to reach the heart (Manousiouthakis et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The SA node is located at the junction of the right atrium and the superior vena cava.
source: The selection of these venous routes is an elegant developmental solution that reflects the anatomical location of the primary cardiac STG targets, which are positioned adjacent to or closest to veins rather than arteries (e.g., the SA node is located at the junction of the right atrium and the superior vena cava).
evidence: This is an anatomical fact based on established knowledge.

claim: A separate subset of STG axons project to the thoracic body wall, the arms, and the dorsal region of the neck, and these follow arteries (specifically, intercostal, subclavian, and vertebral arteries, respectively) to reach these non-cardiac targets.
source: In contrast, a separate subset of STG axons project to the thoracic body wall, the arms, and the dorsal region of the neck, and these follow arteries (specifically, intercostal, subclavian, and vertebral arteries, respectively) to reach these non-cardiac targets.
evidence: This is a descriptive anatomical claim based on the authors' observations.

claim: Edn1-Ednra signaling is a critical axon guidance mechanism that controls the development and ultimate function of the cardiac sympathetic nervous system.
source: Edn1-Ednra signaling, therefore, is a critical axon guidance mechanism that controls the development and ultimate function of the cardiac sympathetic nervous system.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the authors' previous work.

claim: Positive axon guidance alone is insufficient to accomplish correct circuitry.
source: This analysis reveals that positive axon guidance alone is insufficient to accomplish correct circuitry, and defines a molecular mechanism by which axon attraction and repulsion are coordinately controlled to synergistically accomplish proper innervation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: Plexin-A3 (Plxna3) and Plexin-A4 (Plxna4) are expressed in sympathetic neurons.
source: Plexin-A3 (Plxna3) and Plexin-A4 (Plxna4) are expressed in sympathetic neurons (Cheng et al., 2001)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Plxna4 mutant mice display ectopic medial projections from the sympathetic ganglia.
source: and Plxna4 mutant mice display ectopic medial projections from the sympathetic ganglia (Waimey et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Sema3a mutation results in ectopic medial projections from the thoracic sympathetic ganglia, coupled with reduced sympathetic innervation of the heart.
source: Sema3a mutation, and neural crest-specific deletion of Nrp1 (which includes all sympathetic neurons), were also shown to result in ectopic medial projections from the thoracic sympathetic ganglia, coupled with reduced sympathetic innervation of the heart (Ieda et al., 2007; Maden et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Neural crest-specific deletion of Nrp1 results in ectopic medial projections from the thoracic sympathetic ganglia, coupled with reduced sympathetic innervation of the heart.
source: Sema3a mutation, and neural crest-specific deletion of Nrp1 (which includes all sympathetic neurons), were also shown to result in ectopic medial projections from the thoracic sympathetic ganglia, coupled with reduced sympathetic innervation of the heart (Ieda et al., 2007; Maden et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Ednra gene is expressed only in a subset (approx. half) of STG neurons.
source: Because the Ednra gene is expressed only in a subset (approx. half) of STG neurons (Manousiouthakis et al., 2014), the 50% reduction in Plxna4 expression in Ednra-deficient STG could reflect a complete loss of expression in the Ednra+ population, with the gene still expressed in the other half of STG neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Mef2c gene contains an endothelin-dependent MEF2C autoregulatory transcriptional enhancer (Mef2c-F1) element.
source: We previously demonstrated in vivo that myocyte enhance factor Mef2c gene expression in the neural crest lineage is regulated by endothelin (Hu et al., 2015). Specifically, the Mef2c gene contains an endothelin-dependent MEF2C autoregulatory transcriptional enhancer (Mef2c-F1) element (Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Mef2c-F1 enhancer is active in sympathetic chain ganglia at E10.5.
source: Analysis of Mef2c-F1-lacZ transgenic embryos showed that the Mef2c-F1 enhancer is active in sympathetic chain ganglia at E10.5 (Agarwal et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: E9.5 Mef2c-F1-lacZ embryos cultured in the presence of Edn1 peptide exhibited robust induction of β-galactosidase activity within trunk neural crest cell derivatives.
source: Furthermore, E9.5 Mef2c-F1-lacZ embryos cultured in the presence of Edn1 peptide exhibited robust induction of β-galactosidase activity within trunk neural crest cell derivatives (Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Each of the five MEF2 sites in the Plxna4 locus corresponded to regions identified in ChIP-seq as bona fide sites of MEF2C binding.
source: Each of these five MEF2 sites corresponded to regions identified in ChIP-seq as bona fide sites of MEF2C binding (Telese et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data from a previous study.

claim: In the endothelin-dependent subset of cardiac sympathetic axons, Edn1 induces Plxna4 expression via MEF2C to support proper axon guidance.
source: Taken together, these observations are consistent with the interpretation that in the endothelin-dependent subset of cardiac sympathetic axons, Edn1 induces Plxna4 expression via MEF2C to support proper axon guidance
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental data.

claim: Endothelin-independent subsets of STG axons express Plxna4 in a MEF2C-independent manner.
source: whereas endothelin-independent subsets of STG axons express Plxna4 in a MEF2C-independent manner.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental data.

claim: A phenotypic consequence in double heterozygotes when each single heterozygote is normal suggests that the two genes might be functionally related or function in a common pathway.
source: A phenotypic consequence in double heterozygotes when each single heterozygote is normal suggests that the two genes might be functionally related or function in a common pathway.
evidence: This is a general principle of genetic interaction analysis.

claim: A genetic interaction observed in compound heterozygotes suggests that lowering the expression of both gene product together reduces downstream signaling below a threshold level where a phenotype emerges.
source: In any case, a genetic interaction observed in compound heterozygotes suggests that lowering the expression of both gene product together reduces downstream signaling below a threshold level where a phenotype emerges.
evidence: This is a general principle of genetic interaction analysis.

claim: The Ednra and Plxna4 genes are functionally related in cardiac sympathetic axon guidance in a physiologically relevant manner.
source: These observations support the interpretation that the Ednra and Plxna4 genes are coupled in cardiac sympathetic axon guidance in a physiologically relevant manner.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the genetic interaction data.

claim: Amphetamine eventually induces noradrenaline and adrenaline release from the brain and adrenal glands, respectively, which ultimately influence heart rate through systemic circulation.
source: Amphetamine eventually induces noradrenaline and adrenaline release from the brain and adrenal glands, respectively, which ultimately influence heart rate through systemic circulation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of amphetamine's mechanism of action.

claim: The noradrenergic and adrenergic systems in the central nervous system and adrenal glands are intact in double heterozygous mice.
source: This delayed response (monitored 10 min after injection) was fully intact in all double-heterozygous mice (Figure 6b), which demonstrates that the noradrenergic and adrenergic systems in the central nervous system and adrenal glands are intact in double heterozygous mice.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ECG data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The cardiomyocyte-specific components of the conduction system and myocardium that respond to sympathetic inputs are functional in the double-heterozygous background.
source: Furthermore, these mice were normally responsive to the beta-adrenergic receptor agonist isoproterenol (Figure 6c), indicating that the cardiomyocyte-specific components of the conduction system and myocardium that respond to sympathetic inputs are functional in the double-heterozygous background.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ECG data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Sympathetic versus parasympathetic activities can be evaluated by heart rate variability (HRV).
source: Sympathetic versus parasympathetic activities can also be evaluated by heart rate variability (HRV) (Akselrod et al., 1981).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: HRV represents physiological rhythm fluctuations between consecutive beats.
source: HRV represents physiological rhythm fluctuations between consecutive beats: beat-to-beat fluctuation is minimal in the resting state, whereas in the conscious state, the interval between consecutive beats becomes more variable because of fluctuations in the opposing actions of sympathetic and parasympathetic inputs.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of HRV.

claim: Beat-to-beat fluctuation is minimal in the resting state.
source: HRV represents physiological rhythm fluctuations between consecutive beats: beat-to-beat fluctuation is minimal in the resting state, whereas in the conscious state, the interval between consecutive beats becomes more variable because of fluctuations in the opposing actions of sympathetic and parasympathetic inputs.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of HRV.

claim: In the conscious state, the interval between consecutive beats becomes more variable because of fluctuations in the opposing actions of sympathetic and parasympathetic inputs.
source: HRV represents physiological rhythm fluctuations between consecutive beats: beat-to-beat fluctuation is minimal in the resting state, whereas in the conscious state, the interval between consecutive beats becomes more variable because of fluctuations in the opposing actions of sympathetic and parasympathetic inputs.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of HRV.

claim: HRV is divided into low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) components, and commonly described by the LF/HF ratio.
source: HRV is divided into low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) components, and commonly described by the LF/HF ratio (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of HRV analysis.

claim: In Th-Cre; Ednrafl/- mutants, sympathetic innervation and activity are reduced.
source: In Th-Cre; Ednrafl/- mutants, in which sympathetic innervation and activity are reduced (Figure 5d, n–p and w–x)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5d, n-p, and w-x.

claim: Reduced sympathetic innervation in Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/- mice coincides with their reduced LF/HF ratio.
source: Th-Cre; Ednrafl/+; Plxna4+/- ± also exhibited a similar reduction of the LF/HF ratio (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 1b), coinciding with their reduced cardiac sympathetic innervation (Figure 5c, k–m and u–v).
